correctness.rationale: For every binary input, the change set is a forest. Strict majority at changed vertices gives 2b_v-deg(v)>=1; decomposition by cut status and changed endpoints yields Delta J<= c-cut_components<=J_initial-cut_components. The integer cut size k and n-1 edge cap optimize to 2-1/floor(n/2). Order-statistic thresholding commutes with median and finite coarea extends to arbitrary reals. Even-order stars and odd-order singly subdivided stars attain equality; n=2,3 checked separately. Actual check.py passed 84,346 finite binary, 4,320 larger-tree integer-real, and 149 sharpness tests, but these finite tests do not establish the universal theorem.

value.rationale: A motivated exact nonlinear stability question: synchronous neighbor-median filtering on all finite trees can amplify edge variation, unlike asynchronous majority steps. The theorem solves the natural fixed-order maximum exactly for every n, yields a new component-count deficit for each binary update, and extends to all real signals by coarea. The extremal ratio approaches 2 and has explicit parity-sensitive attaining tree geometries. This is a complete sharp family classification rather than a mere finite enumeration or arbitrary parameter slice.
